title: Why Pakistan marks October 27 as Black Day
lines: Every year on the twenty-seventh of October, Pakistan observes Kashmir Black Day.
It marks the arrival of Indian forces in Srinagar in nineteen forty-seven. This year is the seventy-ninth anniversary.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called it the start of a tragic chapter in the history of Jammu and Kashmir.
He said Pakistan's position on Kashmir remains clear, consistent and principled.
President Asif Ali Zardari called for sustained international attention to the situation in the region.
Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said India's measures of the fifth of August, twenty nineteen, could not change the region's disputed status.
He said the dispute cannot be resolved through unilateral actions or the use of force.
The National Assembly unanimously passed a resolution reaffirming Pakistan's moral, political and diplomatic support for Kashmiris.
Pakistan points to United Nations resolutions that call for a plebiscite to decide Kashmir's future.
India rejects Pakistan's position, and considers Jammu and Kashmir an integral part of its territory.
The dispute remains one of the oldest unresolved conflicts in the world, between two nuclear-armed neighbours.
